briefs.explicit:
MISSION BRIEF S-000
Units: metres, seconds, kilograms. Time starts at t = 0 when every robot leaves its start location.

Locations (x, y, zone):
- base: (0, 0), outdoor
- office roof: (89, -81), roof
- storage hall: (143, 78), indoor
- water tank: (-82, 16), outdoor
- parking lot: (78, 29), outdoor

Robots:
- D1 (quadcopter): starts at base. Flies in straight lines at 7 m/s; can reach outdoor and roof locations, not indoor ones. Equipment: camera, cargo carrier (max 2 kg). Endurance: 1200 s, including the return to its start.
- G1 (rover): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 2.5 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 30 kg), camera. Endurance: 4020 s, including the return to its start.
- M1 (mobile_manipulator): starts at base. Drives on the road grid (travel distance = |dx| + |dy|) at 1 m/s; can reach outdoor and indoor locations, not roofs. Equipment: cargo carrier (max 6 kg), robotic arm, camera. Endurance: 3000 s, including the return to its start.

Tasks:
- T1: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 120 s. Needs: camera.
- T2: Photograph parking lot for the condition report. Location: parking lot. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T3: Inspect office roof with a camera. Location: office roof. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera.
- T4: Deliver the toolkit (11 kg) to water tank. Location: water tank. Duration: 30 s. Needs: cargo carrier (payload 11 kg).
- T5: Photograph parking lot for the condition report. Location: parking lot. Duration: 90 s. Needs: camera. Deadline: finished by t = 180 s.

Rules:
1. Every task is done by exactly one robot. A robot does its tasks one at a time, in the order you list them, travelling between task locations.
2. A robot can only do a task if it has the needed equipment, enough payload capacity, and can reach the task location.
3. A task that must start after another task waits until that task is finished, even if a different robot does it.
4. Each robot must be back at its start location before its endurance runs out.
5. Every task must be finished by t = 900 s.

Objective: minimise the finish time of the last task (the makespan).
briefs.informal:
Here's what we need from the robots today.

Positions are in metres from the base at (0, 0). Drones fly straight and can't go indoors; ground robots follow the road grid (so they travel |dx| + |dy|) and can't get onto roofs. Everyone leaves their start spot at time zero.

Places: office roof (89, -81, a rooftop); storage hall (143, 78, indoors); water tank (-82, 16, outside); parking lot (78, 29, outside).

The fleet: D1, a quadcopter waiting at base, carries a camera, cruises at 7 m/s, lifts up to 2 kg and has 20 minutes of flight time, return trip included. G1 is a rover parked at base that hauls up to 30 kg at 2.5 m/s and runs for 67 minutes including the drive back. It has a camera. M1 is our mobile manipulator at base: gripper arm, camera, room for 6 kg, moves at 1 m/s and lasts 50 minutes including getting back.

Jobs:
(T1) Have a look at office roof - that takes 2 minutes on site.
(T2) We need pictures of parking lot for the report - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T3) Have a look at office roof - that takes 1.5 minutes on site.
(T4) Water tank needs the toolkit, which weighs 11 kg - that takes 0.5 minutes on site.
(T5) Document parking lot with pictures - that takes 1.5 minutes on site and it has to be finished within the first 3 minutes.

Everything has to be wrapped up within 15 minutes of the start, and the sooner the last job finishes, the better. Every robot has to make it back to where it started before its battery runs out.
